Citywide Aquatics & Swimming Pools

Where can you swim right now? Every City of Los Angeles pool, on one live schedule: which are open, for lap swim or rec swim, on how many lanes, until when, and which is nearest to you.

Live from each pool's published fall hours. Tap a pool for its full calendar, phone and directions. Lane counts marked as estimates are ours, until the pool tells us.

Every pool, one day

One row per pool, morning to night. Page through the days, or tap a program below the calendar to see only that.

Open it full screen.

What this replaces

  • Twenty-six pages to answer one question. To find a lap swim at 7 tonight, a swimmer opens the year-round pools one at a time. Each types its hours in its own format: a table, a list, a PDF, or a sentence.
  • Status in one place, hours in another. The year-round list says “OPEN, HEATED” or “CLOSED”, and a separate map has current status, but neither has hours. Glassell’s page says “now Open, Heated” while its brochure closes the pool October 22.
  • Hours that have expired, or have no dates. LACES posts August 9 – September 6. Hollywood posts September 13 – 24. Seven pools post hours with no dates at all.
  • The real schedule is in a PDF. Glassell and Westwood publish their hours only in the brochure. Five pools have closures that appear only in the PDF: Celes King III, Glassell, Hubert H. Humphrey, LACES and Van Nuys Sherman Oaks. Three pages still attach last summer’s brochure.
  • “Limited lanes,” never how many. Nine pools say lap lanes are limited, on the page or in the brochure, and none gives a number. The calendars here show lanes: where the pool hasn’t said, the count is our estimate, and one number from the pool makes it exact.
  • The counts disagree with themselves. The aquatics page says “28 seasonal swimming pools, 26 year-round,” and further down “Twenty four pools operate year round” and “Twenty Seven (summer) pools.”
  • One schedule instead. Each pool enters its season once, in a chat or in the calendar. The finder, the citywide day view and the pool’s own page all update together, and a closure ends on its own date.

Admission

Infant (0–2)Free
Children (3–17)$1.00
Adults (18–49)$4.00
50 and up$1.00
Persons with disabilities$1.00
Summer Youth Pass$10
Adult Lap Swim Pass, 30 entries$88
Youth, 50+ and persons with disabilities pass, 30 entries$25
Cash only at the pool. Passes are for year-round pools.
Pool rules and swim attire

Children under 7 must be accompanied by an adult, one to one. Children under 4 need an approved swim diaper. Proper swim attire is required: no cut-offs, street shorts, white T-shirts or rash guards. You must take a swim test before entering the deep end. Full rules on the department's site.

All City aquatics facilities offer accessible ADA pool lifts; many offer universal changing rooms.
